issues.description: The type of the price field for StockIngredient is inconsistent across artifacts: the problem statement (UML) specifies price as int, the template StockIngredient.java defines price as double (and getPrice() returns double), while the solution uses int. This mismatch can confuse students about the expected type and may cause test/signature inconsistencies.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the price type consistent across all artifacts. Preferably update the template StockIngredient to use an int price field and have getPrice() return int to match the UML in the problem statement and the solution (or alternatively update the problem statement and solution to use double if that was intended).

issues.description: The StockIngredient constructor parameter types/signature differ between the problem statement and the template: the UML and solution declare StockIngredient(String, int, int), but the template provides StockIngredient(String, double, int). This inconsistency can mislead students when constructing new StockIngredient instances (and when following the specified API).
issues.suggestedFix: Align the constructor signature in the template with the specification and solution by changing the second parameter type from double to int (i.e., StockIngredient(String name, int price, int quantity)). Ensure parameter types and field types are consistent.

issues.description: The problem statement and the solution expect StockIngredient.price to be an integer (UML and SealSaloon.acceptSupplyDelivery use int price), but the template implementation declares the price field and constructor parameter as double. This mismatch in the expected type for the same conceptual property (ingredient price) will confuse students when they create SealSaloon.acceptSupplyDelivery and instantiate StockIngredient using an int price as required by the spec/solution but the template's constructor expects a double.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the template's StockIngredient use int for the price to match the problem statement and solution: change the price field, constructor parameter, and getPrice() return type from double to int so students can directly instantiate new StockIngredient(name, price, quantity) with an int price.
